question:
A superconducting ring (resistance $R=0$) of self-inductance $L$ is placed in a spatially uniform magnetic field perpendicular to its plane. The external magnetic field varies as $B(t)=B_0\sin(\omega t)$, and the area of the ring is $A$.

Assuming the ring remains superconducting and flux linkage is well defined, find the phase relation between the induced current $i(t)$ in the ring and the external flux $\Phi_{\text{ext}}(t)=AB(t)$. Also find the amplitude $I_0$ of the induced current.

Choose the correct option.

options.A: Current is in phase with $\Phi_{\text{ext}}(t)$ and $I_0=\dfrac{AB_0}{L}$
options.C: Current is $180^\circ$ out of phase with $\Phi_{\text{ext}}(t)$ and $I_0=\dfrac{AB_0}{L}$
